title: Two ways to arrange the same leaves
question: Which stand's foliage reads better to you -- and is the difference worth having as something a plant can inherit?
context_md:
Same species, same bed, same seed, same length of run. **The two stands put down the same amount of leaf** (3,203 against 3,389 cells, within 6%) -- what differs is only how each node's cluster of leaves is *arranged*.

The engine gives a node up to eight leaf cells and then grows them as a random walk, so the shape of every clump is drawn fresh from the dice and nothing has ever controlled it. One of these keeps that; the other makes the clump reach away from the stem in a line instead of bunching.

I am posting this rather than picking, for a specific reason: three previous attempts to give plants different architectures all fired, were counted, and looked identical to you. Those changed which *label* a cell carried. This changes which cells are green, which is why I think it is different in kind -- but that is exactly the claim I keep getting wrong, so it is yours to judge.

**Whichever you prefer can be the default.** The other stays reachable, and because it is a plant's own number rather than a species-wide switch, a line could evolve toward either. If the honest answer is "these look the same", say that -- it is the more useful answer and I would rather retire the lever than keep a knob nobody can see.

items.label: reaching -- leaves line out from the stem
items.caption: same bed, same seed, same number of leaves
